extracted.intended_audience: people interested in creating and submitting math-related online content to the Summer of Math Exposition (SoME) contest
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting an original math-related piece of online content to the Summer of Math Exposition (SoME), within the contest's video / non-video categories and following the contest's eligibility, language, and availability requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness: created for this summer
rubrics_metrics.description: It has to be something new you make this summer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The spirit of this is to encourage people who've never put stuff online before. If you want to work on something you sort of started once before, that's probably fine, but it can't be something you already published before this contest. Optimally, you'd use this as a chance to try something new you otherwise might not have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter: must be about math
rubrics_metrics.description: It has to be about math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Math is meant very broadly; more applied topics like physics or computer science are abundantly welcome. It should be the case that a viewer/reader might come away knowing something mathematical they didn't before.

rubrics_metrics.name: One entry per person/group
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers hope participants make more, but they only have the capacity to judge participants based on a single entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language accessibility: available in English
rubrics_metrics.description: It has to be available in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges will be English speakers, so to be considered for the contest the lesson has to be accessible to them. Translated subtitles on an otherwise non-English video are allowed, but do not necessarily fit this criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: English audio for videos (preferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible, please provide English audio to video content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a request to improve accessibility for the judges, but phrased as a preference rather than an absolute requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and free availability
rubrics_metrics.description: It has to be publicly visible and available for people to consume for free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be freely accessible to the public (not behind paywalls or private).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category split: video vs non-video
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries will be split into video and non-video categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This separation aims to reduce bias from last year, when most entries were videos and reviewers found it difficult to judge video vs non-video formats. The non-video category will still have diverse formats (e.g., games, articles, blog posts) that can be hard to compare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration category
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be a new category for collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers want to encourage more people to work together and will try to pair experts (professors, researchers, or other knowledgeable individuals) with creators. A topic board is on GitHub and collaborations can be discussed on the #collabs channel on Discord.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission and review timeline, including peer review and manual review periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline (subject to change): June 6: submissions open; August 15: submission deadline / start peer review; Sept 1: end peer review / start manual review; Sept 15: finish manual review; Sept 23: announcement video. Process: 10 weeks to submit, 2 weeks for peer review, and 2 weeks for manual review with a panel of judges. Peer review linked entries previously and increased viewership; organizers consider peer review essential and will fix bugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes and subjectivity of judging
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be a cash prize of roughly $1000 for the 'top' entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging decisions are heavily subjective; the point of the competition is to encourage creation rather than emphasize winning.
